text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Multinational oil firms in joint ventures with state-run oil company NNPC cry out over government's reduction of its cash contribution to project costs to $2.05 billion from a $3.32 budget of submitted.
- Lagos state police commissioner, on a tour of police formations indicts his colleagues, saying "most police personnel are armed robbers in police uniform."

- Registration of voters for civilian-rule elections next year dogged by many problems, particularly a shortage of voter cards, said Justice Mamman Nasir, the head of a committee steering the transition from military rule.
- Frenchman Phillipe Troussier named new manager of the Nigerian national soccer team.
- "System failure" at national grid of state-run power company caused Thursday's 10-hour nationwide power cut.
- World Bank cancels $100 million loan for primary education in Nigeria due to poor implementation of the national primary education plan, paper's own investigations show.
- Clashes between two christian religious groups paralyse business in southeastern Calabar town.
- Constant illegal tapping of trees in rubber farms in southeastern Cross River state may force companies out of business, Bassey Edem, managing director of Pamol Rubber Company Nigeria Limited says.

- Nigeria moves to re-negotiate a clause in the agreement setting up the liquefied natural gas (LNG) company to re-acquire the position of managing director which it had ceded to Royal/Dutch Shell group, technical leader constructing the LNG project.
- Central Bank reduces to two percent from five the re-purchasing rate, a development money market operators say could further push down interest rates.

- Ex-finance minister and former secretary to the military government Olu Falae, detained since January in connection with a spate of bomb blasts in the country, is interrogated by a special task force committee investigating the bombings.
- Multinational Mobil Nigeria resumes crude oil drilling at the abandoned Ekpe field in southeastern Nigeria.
